record.original_question: Can every planar graph be drawn in the plane so that every edge is a straight-line segment of integer length?

evidence.quote: Question 8.1 Is it possible to draw every planar graph so that each edge is a line segment of integer length?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A planar graph is a finite simple graph that can be embedded in the Euclidean plane without edge crossings. A straight-line planar drawing of a planar graph G is an assignment of distinct points in the plane to the vertices of G, together with the straight-line segments connecting the images of adjacent vertices, such that no two of these segments cross except at common endpoints. Determine whether the following statement is true: for every planar graph G, there exists a straight-line planar drawing of G in which the Euclidean length of every edge segment is a positive integer.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Harborth's conjecture. It remains unsolved in general, though it has been established for several special classes of planar graphs (bipartite planar graphs, (2,1)-sparse planar graphs, planar graphs of treewidth at most 3, and most recently 4-regular planar graphs, per Chang at GD 2024).

status_evidence.title: Harborth's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Despite much subsequent research, Harborth's conjecture remains unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Harborth's Conjecture for 4-Regular Planar Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Every 4-regular planar graph has a straight-line embedding in the plane where all edges have integer length.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: settled for 4-regular planar graphs (GD 2024).
